problem: How can tasks resume without workers overwriting newer progress?
principle: Persist tenant/task-scoped checkpoints and compare versions. External effects require separate reconciliation.
check: Does a checkpoint guarantee one email?
answer: No. An unknown receipt requires external query/idempotency or manual reconciliation.

procedures.state: State schema, nodes/versions, pending tasks and checkpoint ID.
procedures.failure: Uncommitted work can replay; external effects need separate deduplication.
procedures.measure: Crash before/after nodes; inspect resume point and remote write count.
procedures.case: Reuse saved quotations; recompute an incomplete comparison.

procedures.state: Task ID, version, lease and fencing token where required.
procedures.failure: Zero updated rows means lost ownership; stale workers cannot overwrite.
procedures.measure: Only one writer commits at the same expected version; stale versions fail. Test leases/fencing separately.
procedures.case: Two workers read v7; one writes v8 and the other reloads.

procedures.state: operation_id, request fingerprint, state and receipt.
procedures.failure: Reject changed payloads under one key; escalate without query/dedup support.
procedures.measure: Lose a success response; verify restart creates no duplicate.
procedures.case: Find draft-42 by original key after a timed-out creation.

scope: The code implements tenant-scoped SQLite versioned checkpoints and CAS. Lease expiry/fencing and external idempotency/reconciliation are additional execution mechanisms.
